data.title: C018: finite-closure certificate wire epoch 2 carries the model; kernel re-derives the successor relation (bn-35y4f + bn-1m952)

data.body: low (labelling, not soundness): every receipt now reports checker.version +wire.CONTCERT.2 and wire_epoch_id CONTCERT/2, also for an epoch-1 certificate. The epoch-1 receipt stays distinguishable through trusted_components (certificate-model-correspondence) and claim.text, so no epoch-1 claim reads as model-bound. Consider writing the certificate's own epoch into the receipt (e.g. from CheckedClaim::wire_epoch) so a reader of checker.version alone is not misled. Non-blocking.

info: evaluator depth exhaustion returns Fault::Overflow, which check_model_closure maps to Rejected(EvaluationOverflow). It is unreachable today, because the decoder bounds depth at MAX_EXPRESSION_DEPTH with the same counting (probe: depth 32 verifies, 33 and 10000 are Unsupported(ExpressionDepth)). If the decoder invariant ever weakens, this would be a false Reject, not Unsupported (INV-008). A distinct Fault variant mapped to Unsupported(ResourceBound) would fail typed. Non-blocking.

data.reason: Kernel review (GOV 4, second non-author reviewer). No soundness defect found. Decoder grammar, canonicity (names, outcomes by bytes, assignments, initials, fairness by (strength, scope)) and the evaluator (checked i64, no short-circuit, pre-state assignments, frame rule, domain fault, depth 32 counted as in model-core) match continuum-model-core. Rows must equal the re-derived, sorted and deduplicated rows exactly. Init(M) must be in S, S in Dom(M), and the invariant is resolved by name and evaluated at every table state. An epoch-1 claim keeps certificate-model-correspondence and has no model_identity. The precharge runs before any evaluation. The kernel has no dependencies and no unsafe code, and check_crate_boundaries reports 0 violations. Tests: kernel-core, 4 engine-reference differential/corpus/wire suites, c018_checker_mutation and pr16_impl02 all pass. Probes: 9125 single-byte mutants gave 300 verified, and an independent Python decoder/evaluator confirms all 300 true (215 of them change the model and verify a true claim about the changed model). 6000 random model-bound certificates gave 0 disagreements with that oracle. Depth and model-bytes bounds are typed Unsupported. There are 2 non-blocking comments (receipt epoch label, and the unreachable depth-exhaustion mapping). Residual as disclosed: the daemon does not yet compare the carried model with its own model, so the binding is envelope-digest-binding (trusted).

[risk:high] Failure modes: false relation or invariant acceptance, malformed-input panic, resource exhaustion, epoch-assurance confusion, or an unbound carried model. Edge cases: legacy epoch 1, duplicate or unordered rows, out-of-range indices, arithmetic overflow, domain escape, unknown predicates, and model, depth, node, certificate, or work limits. Rollback: revert b46ad70dfac6199cfb700a95ec70ef7e6bba70be and retain epoch-1 decoding; published artifacts remain immutable. Monitoring: count verdicts by wire epoch, rejection reason, and resource; track checker latency and memory; alert on envelope-binding failures when the system path implements that check. Validation: reviewed the full persisted range 27d378b9b243f8e893b3f0c441252409ded6895c..b46ad70dfac6199cfb700a95ec70ef7e6bba70be across all changed files, including decoder, evaluator, checker, emitter, receipt, daemon consumer, tests, governance evidence, and migration text. No security blocker found. This commit-scoped LGTM does not establish daemon model binding, runtime qualification, release readiness, or risk:critical human approval.
